title: Button Class Name
prompt: A React button component needs a predictable className from its props. Write a helper that returns "btn btn-primary" when variant is "primary", "btn btn-secondary" when variant is "secondary", and adds " btn-disabled" when disabled is true.

explanation.beginner:
Example: buttonClassName({"variant":"primary"}) produces "btn btn-primary". Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Compare “builds secondary disabled class names”: input [{"variant":"secondary","disabled":true}] produces "btn btn-secondary btn-disabled". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Tempting mistake: Capitalization, whitespace, and boolean-versus-string output are part of the contract; truthiness alone may combine distinct states.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “builds secondary disabled class names”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
